Set a bounded timeout and an overall work budget; a library socket timeout is not necessarily a total end-to-end deadline. Limit response size, page count and items processed for untrusted or unexpectedly large responses.

Follow the documented pagination mechanism and validate that next-page destinations stay within the approved service. Deduplicate using stable identifiers where the API contract and data changes can produce repeated items.

Retry only appropriate transient failures with bounded backoff and server guidance such as Retry-After. A timeout after a write does not prove the write failed; use API-supported idempotency or reconciliation before retrying a mutation.
notes.worked_example: Against a local mock endpoint, with urllib.request.urlopen("http://127.0.0.1:8000/assets?page=1", timeout=5) as response: payload = json.load(response). Catch urllib.error.HTTPError, urllib.error.URLError and json.JSONDecodeError at an appropriate boundary, then validate that payload contains the documented items array.
notes.practice: Implement a read-only mock client with three pages, one transient error and a malformed JSON response. Set maximum pages and attempts and record why each retry is permitted; never include access tokens in logs.
notes.check_question: Why is automatically retrying a timed-out create request unsafe?
notes.check_answer: The server may have completed the creation before the response was lost, so a retry can create a duplicate unless the API provides idempotency or the client first reconciles the outcome.

notes.topic: Node.js Async Work, Promises and Error Boundaries
notes.content: Node.js uses an event loop and asynchronous I/O to handle work without waiting synchronously for each network or filesystem operation. async/await makes promise-based flow readable but does not make CPU-heavy code non-blocking or automatically handle rejected operations.
notes.source_title: Node.js Learn: Do not block the event loop
notes.case_study: Illustrative scenario: A local report endpoint becomes unresponsive while a large synchronous calculation runs; the learner distinguishes CPU work from I/O and limits the dataset before considering a worker design.
key_points: An async function returns a promise; await pauses that function until settlement while other scheduled work may continue. Catch expected failures and propagate unexpected ones to an explicit boundary.
Use try/finally for cleanup when a resource must be released. Avoid swallowing exceptions or logging success after a failed operation.

Promise.all can run independent work concurrently but rejects when one input rejects; Promise.allSettled records each outcome. Neither imposes a concurrency limit or cancels all underlying work automatically.

Limit concurrency and input size to avoid exhausting sockets, memory or downstream services. Long synchronous loops and JSON processing can still block the event loop; use supported worker approaches when justified.
notes.worked_example: In a local script, const results = await Promise.allSettled([readFile("a.json", "utf8"), readFile("b.json", "utf8")]); then inspect every status before parsing successful values. The missing-file result must remain visible rather than being replaced silently with an empty report.
notes.practice: Create two small synthetic files and one missing path. Compare sequential await, Promise.all and Promise.allSettled, record each failure path and add a maximum batch size.
notes.check_question: Does adding async to a CPU-intensive function prevent it from blocking the Node.js event loop?
notes.check_answer: No. Synchronous CPU work still runs on the event-loop thread unless it is explicitly moved to a suitable worker or otherwise redesigned.

notes.topic: Node.js Packages, Configuration and a Local HTTP Service
notes.content: A maintainable Node.js service has explicit dependencies, predictable configuration and controlled handling of requests and failures. Keep a training service bound to loopback, validate input and use supported runtime and package versions.
notes.case_study: Illustrative scenario: A local training API serves synthetic inventory data while refusing unsupported methods and oversized input; its package lockfile makes the dependency selection reviewable.
key_points: package.json declares scripts, metadata and dependencies; commit the appropriate lockfile and use npm ci for an existing consistent lockfile. Review package sources, lifecycle scripts and advisories rather than treating a successful install as a trust guarantee.
Choose CommonJS or ECMAScript modules deliberately and make package settings and file extensions consistent. Runtime versions affect available APIs and support status.

Read non-secret configuration from a documented source and validate ports, hosts and limits at startup. Store secrets through the approved mechanism and avoid putting them into repository files, responses or logs.

Validate request method, path, content type and bounded body size; set deliberate timeouts and return a controlled error response. A minimal local example lacks production authentication, TLS termination, rate controls and operational supervision.
notes.worked_example: A loopback-only ESM example uses import { createServer } from "node:http"; const server = createServer((req,res) => { if (req.method !== "GET" || req.url !== "/health") { res.writeHead(404); res.end(); return; } res.writeHead(200,{"Content-Type":"application/json"}); res.end(JSON.stringify({status:"ok"})); }); server.listen(3000,"127.0.0.1"); Add an error handler before listening and test with curl --max-time 5 http://127.0.0.1:3000/health.
notes.practice: In a dedicated lab directory, build a local /health endpoint and test the expected route, unknown path, unsupported method and occupied port. Document configuration and dependencies without deploying it publicly.
notes.check_question: Why should a local learning server bind explicitly to 127.0.0.1?
notes.check_answer: It limits ordinary network reachability to the same host and reduces accidental exposure while the learning example lacks a complete deployment security design.

flashcards.question: Why is hexadecimal commonly used in operations tooling?
flashcards.answer: It provides a compact human-readable representation of binary values used in memory addresses, packets and logs.

flashcards.question: What does O(n log n) indicate?
flashcards.answer: The runtime grows proportionally to n log n, typical of efficient divide-and-conquer algorithms.

flashcards.question: Why use version control for scripts?
flashcards.answer: It preserves history, supports peer review, and enables safe rollback of operational automation.

flashcards.question: What is ECC memory used for?
flashcards.answer: It detects and corrects certain memory errors, improving reliability in critical systems.

flashcards.question: Why choose RAID 10 over RAID 5 for some workloads?
flashcards.answer: RAID 10 often improves random-write performance and avoids parity-update overhead, but usable capacity and failure tolerance differ. With paired mirrors it can survive one failure per pair; losing both members of one pair can lose data. RAID is not backup.

flashcards.question: What is the purpose of hot-aisle/cold-aisle design?
flashcards.answer: To improve airflow efficiency and reduce recirculation of hot exhaust air.

flashcards.question: What does subnetting primarily achieve?
flashcards.answer: It divides an address range into smaller prefixes for allocation and routing. Separate Layer 2 broadcast domains require matching VLAN or physical design; subnetting alone does not isolate Ethernet broadcasts.

flashcards.question: What does STP prevent?
flashcards.answer: Layer 2 loops that can create broadcast storms and MAC table instability.

flashcards.question: When is single-mode fiber preferred?
flashcards.answer: For long-distance, high-bandwidth links with lower attenuation requirements.

flashcards.question: What role does NTP play in operations?
flashcards.answer: It synchronizes time across systems, critical for logging, security, and correlation.

flashcards.question: What does BPDU Guard protect against?
flashcards.answer: It protects an edge port from unexpected BPDUs by placing the port into a protective state, commonly error-disabled on Cisco IOS. Investigate the attached device before recovery; do not apply endpoint assumptions to legitimate uplinks.

flashcards.question: How does FortiLink help operations?
flashcards.answer: It centralizes FortiSwitch management and policy orchestration through FortiGate.

flashcards.question: What is least-privilege firewall design?
flashcards.answer: Only explicitly required traffic is allowed; everything else is denied by policy.

flashcards.question: Why are rollback steps required in a MOP?
flashcards.answer: They enable safe recovery if a planned change causes service risk.

flashcards.question: Why centralize OS logs?
flashcards.answer: To improve monitoring, forensic analysis, and incident response consistency.

flashcards.question: What is the value of patch windows?
flashcards.answer: They reduce risk by coordinating updates, validation checks and rollback planning.

flashcards.question: Why practice restore drills?
flashcards.answer: To verify backup integrity and confirm recovery objectives are achievable.

flashcards.question: Why can accuracy alone be misleading?
flashcards.answer: Class imbalance may hide poor recall/precision for critical incident classes.

flashcards.question: What is model drift?
flashcards.answer: Changes in data distributions or relationships can make a deployed model less suitable and degrade performance. Monitor both input changes and measured outcomes; a detected distribution shift is not itself proof of a performance loss.

flashcards.question: Why is responsible AI important in operations?
flashcards.answer: It reduces bias, strengthens trust, and supports accountable decision-making.

flashcards.question: What makes a strong shift handover?
flashcards.answer: Clear status, risk summary, pending actions, owners, and supporting evidence.

flashcards.question: Why use severity matrices in incident triage?
flashcards.answer: They standardize escalation decisions and speed response under pressure.

flashcards.question: What does root cause analysis aim to do?
flashcards.answer: Eliminate underlying causes so incidents do not repeatedly recur.

flashcards.question: Why are communication skills critical for operations engineers?
flashcards.answer: Effective communication reduces misalignment and accelerates coordinated response.

flashcards.question: Why define acceptance criteria early?
flashcards.answer: They provide objective measures for validating project success.

flashcards.question: What is the purpose of post-project evaluation?
flashcards.answer: To compare outcomes to requirements and identify actionable improvements.

flashcards.question: What decimal value does 11111111 represent as unsigned and as signed 8-bit two’s-complement?
flashcards.answer: Unsigned: 255. Signed two’s-complement: −1, because the most significant bit has weight −128 and the other bits total 127.

flashcards.question: Why is binary search unsuitable for an unsorted list?
flashcards.answer: Each comparison discards half the search interval only because ordering proves the target cannot be in that half. Without sorted data that assumption is invalid.

flashcards.question: Why should duplicate asset IDs be checked before building a dictionary?
flashcards.answer: Assigning a second value to the same key replaces the first, hiding conflicting records and making the resulting inventory appear cleaner than its input.

flashcards.question: Why separate file parsing from the calculation function?
flashcards.answer: A pure calculation can be tested with small known inputs without filesystem setup; parsing errors and arithmetic errors can then be diagnosed independently.

flashcards.question: What does git diff --staged show?
flashcards.answer: The changes currently staged for the next commit, compared with HEAD. Unstaged edits require a separate git diff review.

flashcards.question: Which test distinguishes usage > 80 from usage >= 80?
flashcards.answer: Exactly 80%. Both conditions agree on values below or above the threshold, so the boundary case reveals the difference.

flashcards.question: Why does a component fitting a slot not prove it is supported?
flashcards.answer: Electrical lanes, power, firmware, protocol and vendor compatibility constraints may differ despite matching physical dimensions.

flashcards.question: How many physical cores are in a two-socket system with 12 cores per socket and two threads per core?
flashcards.answer: 24 physical cores and 48 logical processors when simultaneous multithreading is enabled.

flashcards.question: Does ECC mean all possible memory corruption is corrected?
flashcards.answer: No. Correction and detection capabilities are limited by the ECC implementation; some multi-bit faults remain uncorrectable and need escalation.

flashcards.question: Why is RAID 10’s two-disk failure tolerance dependent on which disks fail?
flashcards.answer: Its data is mirrored in pairs. Losing one disk in each of two pairs can survive; losing both members of one pair loses that pair’s data.

flashcards.question: Why do two power supplies plugged into the same power path leave a shared risk?
flashcards.answer: A failure in that shared upstream path can remove both supplies. Redundancy must be evaluated across the entire path, with adequate remaining capacity.

flashcards.question: Does a green SMART health status prove a disk is reliable?
flashcards.answer: No. SMART exposes selected health indicators and thresholds; faults can occur without prior warning, so use backups, monitoring and corroborating evidence.

flashcards.question: Which destination MAC does a host normally use when sending to an IPv4 address outside its subnet?
flashcards.answer: The local default gateway’s MAC address, resolved using ARP. The packet’s destination IP remains the remote host’s address.

flashcards.question: What is the network and broadcast address for 192.0.2.77/27?
flashcards.answer: The block size is 32. The address lies in .64–.95, so the network is 192.0.2.64 and broadcast is 192.0.2.95.

flashcards.question: Why can an IPv6 address contain :: at most once?
flashcards.answer: Two compressed runs would make it ambiguous how many zero groups belong in each position when expanding the address to eight groups.

flashcards.question: Why can two correctly addressed hosts in VLAN 20 fail across a switch-to-switch link?
flashcards.answer: Their Layer 2 path may be broken: VLAN 20 could be missing, disallowed on the trunk, or blocked by another fault. Correct IP settings do not establish VLAN forwarding.

flashcards.question: Which route matches 192.0.2.100 most specifically: /0, 192.0.2.0/24 or 192.0.2.64/26?
flashcards.answer: 192.0.2.64/26, covering .64–.127. Its 26-bit prefix is more specific than /24 or /0.

flashcards.question: What does a successful IP ping fail to demonstrate about DNS?
flashcards.answer: It does not prove the configured resolver is reachable or that the correct name resolves. Test the name and inspect the DNS response separately.

flashcards.question: Why does strong Wi-Fi signal not guarantee high throughput?
flashcards.answer: Airtime contention, interference, retransmissions, channel width, client capability and wired bottlenecks can limit throughput despite good received signal strength.

flashcards.question: What is the raw loss budget for transmit minimum −4 dBm and receive sensitivity −14 dBm?
flashcards.answer: 10 dB: −4 − (−14) = 10. Reserve the required engineering margin and also verify maximum receiver input and the manufacturer’s reach limits.

flashcards.question: Why is BPDU Guard normally used on edge ports rather than normal switch uplinks?
flashcards.answer: Edge ports should not receive BPDUs. Uplinks normally exchange them, so applying the same guard there can disable a legitimate path.
flashcards.topic: Cisco Switch Hardening and Access Security

flashcards.question: What is a port’s PVID used for in a typical VLAN-aware switch?
flashcards.answer: It assigns incoming untagged traffic to a VLAN. Egress tagging and VLAN membership still need checking separately against the model’s manual.

flashcards.question: Does a healthy FortiLink prove that an attached endpoint can reach an application?
flashcards.answer: No. It shows the management relationship is operating; endpoint VLAN membership, addressing, routing and firewall policy still require verification.

flashcards.question: Why should a firewall test include a prohibited flow as well as the required flow?
flashcards.answer: Successful required traffic proves availability, while a denied test checks that the new rule has not granted unintended access.

flashcards.question: Why can redundant gateways fail to provide end-to-end availability?
flashcards.answer: A shared upstream link, power source, switch, application dependency or configuration fault can still affect both paths. Resilience must cover the service’s full dependency chain.

flashcards.question: What is the practical difference between shaping and policing?
flashcards.answer: Shaping generally buffers and delays excess traffic to smooth its rate; policing enforces a rate by dropping or remarking excess traffic, according to configuration.

flashcards.question: How do you convert an interface octet-counter difference into average bit/s?
flashcards.answer: Multiply the byte difference by 8 and divide by elapsed seconds, handling resets or wraparound before interpreting the result.

flashcards.question: Why must rollback criteria be written before beginning a change?
flashcards.answer: They establish an agreed stopping point and recovery action before time pressure or partial failure makes decisions harder, and reserve enough time to recover.

flashcards.question: Why does an active systemd unit not prove that users can access an application?
flashcards.answer: The process may be running while its listener, dependencies, network path or application behaviour is faulty; test the actual service separately.
flashcards.topic: Linux Process, Service and Package Management

flashcards.question: Why should a baseline be tested before applying it to a server?
flashcards.answer: A setting can reduce risk while also breaking a required role or application, so compatibility and recovery must be established first.

flashcards.question: Which control failed if a validly authenticated trainee can delete production backups?
flashcards.answer: Authorization or privilege design failed: authentication only established the identity, not whether that action should be allowed.

flashcards.question: Why can a backup job report success while recovery is still unsuccessful?
flashcards.answer: The backup may omit dependencies, contain inconsistent data, be inaccessible, or take too long to restore; a job result does not validate end-to-end recovery.

flashcards.question: What does idempotence mean for a configuration script?
flashcards.answer: Repeating the operation converges on the same intended state without unintended additional changes.

flashcards.question: Why must incident notes distinguish observations from hypotheses?
flashcards.answer: It prevents an untested explanation being treated as fact and helps the next responder choose evidence that can confirm or reject it.

flashcards.question: Why compare a machine learning model with a simple baseline?
flashcards.answer: The baseline shows whether added complexity delivers a useful measurable improvement for the task.

flashcards.question: Why is fitting a scaler on the full dataset a form of leakage?
flashcards.answer: The training pipeline learns information from held-out data, so evaluation no longer represents a truly unseen dataset.

flashcards.question: Can a 99% accurate detector be useless when only 1% of events are incidents?
flashcards.answer: Yes. Predicting every event as normal achieves 99% accuracy while detecting no incidents.

flashcards.question: Why is a human review step insufficient by itself?
flashcards.answer: Reviewers need authority, time, relevant information and a usable challenge process; automatic acceptance of suggestions provides little control.

flashcards.question: What is the difference between data drift and model performance degradation?
flashcards.answer: Data drift is a change in input distribution; performance degradation is worse task outcomes. Either can occur without immediately proving the other.

flashcards.question: Why does an anomaly score not prove that equipment has failed?
flashcards.answer: An unusual pattern can result from legitimate workload changes, sensor faults or new operating conditions and needs corroborating evidence.

flashcards.question: What should a trainee do if an approved procedure does not match the equipment or conditions?
flashcards.answer: Stop the task safely and escalate to the designated supervisor rather than improvising.

flashcards.question: Which four details make a pending handover action usable?
flashcards.answer: A clear action, named owner, due or review time, and reference to the relevant evidence or ticket.

flashcards.question: Why should an incident be escalated before its root cause is known?
flashcards.answer: Impact, risk or elapsed time can require additional support immediately; establishing root cause is not a prerequisite for escalation.

flashcards.question: Why is a screenshot alone often weak evidence?
flashcards.answer: It may omit context, time, identity, approval and the relationship to the stated outcome; accompany it with a clear explanation and traceable record.

flashcards.question: What should an update say when a recovery time cannot yet be estimated?
flashcards.answer: State that the recovery time is unconfirmed, explain the current action and give the next update time.

flashcards.question: What turns a reflection into an actionable development plan?
flashcards.answer: A specific change in behaviour or skill, a completion date and evidence showing whether the change improved the outcome.

flashcards.question: Why does technical ability to access data not establish permission to use it?
flashcards.answer: Authorisation, purpose and confidentiality obligations determine permitted use; an overly broad access setting does not remove those duties.

flashcards.question: How can a team resolve competing technical explanations constructively?
flashcards.answer: Express them as testable hypotheses, agree safe evidence collection and compare results against predicted outcomes.

flashcards.question: Why is "operator error" usually an incomplete root-cause conclusion?
flashcards.answer: It does not explain why the system permitted or failed to catch the error, such as unclear procedures, missing validation or inadequate access controls.
flashcards.topic: Problem Solving and Root Cause Analysis

flashcards.question: What is the difference between task effort and duration?
flashcards.answer: Effort is the amount of work required; duration is elapsed calendar time including waits, scheduling and availability.

flashcards.question: If utilisation rises from 40% to 50%, what are the percentage-point and relative increases?
flashcards.answer: It rises by 10 percentage points and by 25% relative to the original 40%.

flashcards.question: Why should a report include limitations?
flashcards.answer: They show where the evidence does not support a stronger conclusion and help the reader judge whether further work is needed.

flashcards.question: Why is "make the system user friendly" a weak acceptance criterion?
flashcards.answer: It is ambiguous until linked to a defined user task and measurable success condition.

flashcards.question: Why can an authoritative source still be unsuitable for a decision?
flashcards.answer: It may address a different version, environment, population or purpose, so applicability must be checked as well as authority.

flashcards.question: Why document a rejected design option?
flashcards.answer: It preserves the evidence and trade-offs behind the decision so future reviewers can reassess it when constraints change.

flashcards.question: Why is "code written" insufficient as a definition of done?
flashcards.answer: The work may still lack required behaviour, tests, review, documentation or integration needed for a usable increment.

flashcards.question: What does a passed test establish?
flashcards.answer: That the observed behaviour matched the expected result for that test and conditions, not that every possible fault is absent.

flashcards.question: How does evaluation differ from a feature list?
flashcards.answer: It judges how well the delivered work solved the defined problem using evidence, including weaknesses and trade-offs.

flashcards.question: Does a router preserve the original Ethernet source MAC across routed hops?
flashcards.answer: No. It creates a new link-layer frame for the outgoing link; the end-to-end IP addresses normally remain unchanged unless a mechanism such as NAT modifies them.

flashcards.question: Does UDP guarantee that datagrams arrive in order?
flashcards.answer: No. Applications must tolerate loss, duplication or reordering or implement their own handling when needed.
flashcards.topic: TCP, UDP, Ports and Connection State

flashcards.question: Why is 192.0.2.80/27 not a valid /27 network boundary?
flashcards.answer: A /27 advances in blocks of 32. .80 is inside .64–.95; its network is .64, not .80.

flashcards.question: Why can a switch behave differently after a reboot even though a configuration worked earlier?
flashcards.answer: A running configuration change may not have been saved to startup configuration, or boot behaviour may select a different configuration. Compare the active and persistent state.
flashcards.topic: First Switch Setup: Console, Identity and Baseline

flashcards.question: Why can an SVI with a correct IP address still be unreachable?
flashcards.answer: Its VLAN may lack an active forwarding path, a trunk may omit the VLAN, the gateway may be wrong, or ACL/management policy may block the traffic. Check Layer 2 state and routing as well as the IP.
flashcards.topic: Management VLAN, SVI and SSH Access

flashcards.question: Does a locally configured trunk guarantee a VLAN can cross the link?
flashcards.answer: No. The peer, VLAN existence, allowed lists, native-VLAN behaviour and forwarding state must also agree.

flashcards.question: Can an endpoint use a default gateway address from a different conventional subnet?
flashcards.answer: Normally no. Its next hop must be directly reachable on its local link under the configured addressing design; use a gateway inside that VLAN’s subnet.

flashcards.question: Will two 1 Gb/s LACP links necessarily give one file transfer 2 Gb/s?
flashcards.answer: No. Typical per-flow hashing selects one member, so aggregate capacity across multiple flows can increase while one flow remains on a single member.

flashcards.question: What does STP root placement influence?
flashcards.answer: It influences the calculated forwarding topology and blocked paths for the spanning-tree instance, affecting traffic paths and failover behaviour.
flashcards.topic: STP Root Placement and Edge Protection

flashcards.question: Must OSPF process IDs match between neighbours on Cisco IOS?
flashcards.answer: No. The process ID is locally significant. Neighbours still need compatible area, link and protocol parameters.
flashcards.topic: Single-Area OSPF Setup and Adjacency Diagnosis

flashcards.question: Why can a carefully written deny rule have no observed effect?
flashcards.answer: An earlier permit may match first, or the ACL may be applied to the wrong interface/direction. Examine order, attachment and counters.
flashcards.topic: IPv4 ACLs: Wildcards, Direction and Verification

flashcards.question: Does a working NAT translation show that a least-privilege firewall policy is configured?
flashcards.answer: No. Translation establishes address/port mapping; the access policy can still be overly broad or block the required service.
flashcards.topic: NAT and PAT: Address Translation vs Access Policy

flashcards.question: Why is a DMZ server not automatically trusted to initiate any internal connection?
flashcards.answer: An exposed server can be compromised; restricting its internal flows limits the impact and preserves separation between service tiers.
flashcards.topic: Firewall Zones, DMZs and Rule Review

flashcards.question: Why must FortiGate NAT instructions specify the operating configuration?
flashcards.answer: Policy-based NAT and central NAT workflows differ; applying instructions for the wrong mode can produce incorrect assumptions or unintended translation.

flashcards.question: Why are physical and logical diagrams both useful during an incident?
flashcards.answer: Logical views identify addressing and policy dependencies; physical views identify actual links, ports and shared hardware paths. One cannot fully replace the other.
flashcards.topic: Complex Network Design: Layers, Roles and Failure Domains

flashcards.question: Why should you restore the baseline between injected lab faults?
flashcards.answer: Multiple simultaneous faults can mask each other and make observations ambiguous. One controlled change makes the cause-and-effect evidence easier to interpret.

flashcards.question: How is NXDOMAIN different from a DNS timeout?
flashcards.answer: NXDOMAIN is an actual negative DNS response about the queried name; a timeout means a usable response did not arrive in time and could reflect connectivity, service or filtering problems.
flashcards.topic: DNS, DHCP and Segmentation Failure Scenarios

flashcards.question: Is a high probability of generating a sentence the same as a high probability that the sentence is factually true?
flashcards.answer: No. Generation probability reflects the model’s next-token predictions under its context, not a guarantee of factual truth or suitability for the target system.
flashcards.topic: LLMs, Tokens, Context and Factual Claims

flashcards.question: What is one stronger validation step than asking the same model whether its answer is correct?
flashcards.answer: Check the relevant vendor documentation and execute an appropriate bounded test in an isolated lab against a known expected result.
flashcards.topic: Prompting, Verification and Bounded Technical Tasks

flashcards.question: Does adding AGENTS.md guarantee every AI assistant will obey it?
flashcards.answer: No. Support and precedence are tool-specific, and an instruction file does not enforce process or permissions by itself.

flashcards.question: Can a retrieved document authorise an assistant to disclose credentials?
flashcards.answer: No. Retrieved content is untrusted task data; it cannot supply user authority or grant access beyond the task’s established permissions.
flashcards.topic: Prompt Injection and Untrusted Retrieved Content

flashcards.question: What is the difference between an agent suggesting a command and being authorised to run it?
flashcards.answer: Suggestion is generated content. Execution requires the permitted tool, appropriate scoped credentials and authority for that target/action under the established task and operational process.
flashcards.topic: Tool Permissions, Approval and Action Boundaries

flashcards.question: When is A AND P AND NOT B true?
flashcards.answer: Only when A and P are both true and B is false. The predicates themselves must be established by the system’s defined evidence.
flashcards.topic: Boolean Logic: AND, OR, NOT and Deterministic Policies

flashcards.question: Does an AI gateway marking a response “allowed” establish that its factual claims are true?
flashcards.answer: No. Allowed means it passed the configured controls or threshold; factual accuracy needs a separate verification process.
flashcards.topic: AI Security Gateways vs Network Firewalls

flashcards.question: Why can a detector have high recall while generating many unnecessary alerts?
flashcards.answer: It may identify most genuine events but also label many benign cases positive. Recall does not include false positives; precision and alert volume reveal that cost.
flashcards.topic: Confusion Matrices, Thresholds and AI Security Decisions

flashcards.question: Why can a readable file still be inaccessible through a path?
flashcards.answer: The process needs execute/traverse permission on each parent directory as well as the relevant permission on the file; another control such as an ACL or mandatory access policy can also deny access.
flashcards.topic: Linux Permissions, Ownership, umask and ACLs

flashcards.question: If ping succeeds but an HTTP request fails, is the network healthy?
flashcards.answer: Only an ICMP response has been demonstrated. The target port, listener, firewall, TLS or application may still be faulty.
flashcards.topic: Linux Network Diagnostics from Interface to Application

flashcards.question: Why does free space reported by vgs not prove that an application filesystem has free space?
flashcards.answer: vgs reports unallocated volume-group capacity. The logical volume and filesystem used by the application may still be full until an approved, supported allocation and filesystem change is performed.
flashcards.topic: Linux Filesystems, Inodes, Mounts and LVM

flashcards.question: What is the difference between a user public key and a server host key?
flashcards.answer: The user key authenticates a client account to the server; the host key lets the client verify the identity of the server.
flashcards.topic: SSH Keys, Host Verification and Secure Remote Access

flashcards.question: Why can a script succeed manually but fail as a scheduled task?
flashcards.answer: The scheduler can provide a different account, working directory, PATH, environment, permissions or network availability; reproduce those conditions when diagnosing it.
flashcards.topic: Scheduled Work with cron and systemd Timers

flashcards.question: Why is repeatedly restarting a failing service a weak diagnostic approach?
flashcards.answer: It can erase useful context, add load or hide the underlying dependency or resource issue; inspect the recorded failure and establish a testable explanation first.
flashcards.topic: systemd Units, Journals and Resource Diagnosis

flashcards.question: Why does a flexible document schema still require design and validation?
flashcards.answer: Applications depend on consistent meanings and usable queries; uncontrolled types, names and nesting create correctness and maintenance problems even if the database accepts the documents.
flashcards.topic: MongoDB Document Modelling and Schema Decisions

flashcards.question: Why can updateOne report matchedCount 1 and modifiedCount 0?
flashcards.answer: A document matched the filter but already contained the requested value, so no data change was needed.
flashcards.topic: MongoDB CRUD, Filters and Update Semantics

flashcards.question: Why is a lower query time from one tiny test insufficient evidence for an index decision?
flashcards.answer: Timings vary with caching and measurement noise, and the dataset or workload may not be representative; examine plans, scanned counts, repeatable workload results and write costs.
flashcards.topic: MongoDB Indexes and explain for Query Diagnosis

flashcards.question: Why is binding to localhost not a substitute for authentication in a shared environment?
flashcards.answer: Other processes or users on the host can potentially reach that listener; network binding limits reachability but does not establish a permitted database identity and role.
flashcards.topic: MongoDB Secure Connectivity and Service Boundaries

flashcards.question: Why is an exported JSON file not necessarily a complete MongoDB backup?
flashcards.answer: It does not capture every database object and recovery property such as all indexes, metadata, users or a consistent multi-collection point in time; the intended recovery requirements determine the needed backup method.
flashcards.topic: MongoDB Backup, Restore and Recovery Validation

flashcards.question: Why should an inventory script validate every row before writing a combined output?
flashcards.answer: It can detect inconsistent or partial input before producing a misleading result; the script can then fail clearly or follow an explicitly documented partial-result policy.
flashcards.topic: Python Automation with CSV, JSON and Validated Inputs

flashcards.question: Why is automatically retrying a timed-out create request unsafe?
flashcards.answer: The server may have completed the creation before the response was lost, so a retry can create a duplicate unless the API provides idempotency or the client first reconciles the outcome.
flashcards.topic: Python HTTP APIs, Timeouts, Pagination and Idempotence

flashcards.question: Does adding async to a CPU-intensive function prevent it from blocking the Node.js event loop?
flashcards.answer: No. Synchronous CPU work still runs on the event-loop thread unless it is explicitly moved to a suitable worker or otherwise redesigned.
flashcards.topic: Node.js Async Work, Promises and Error Boundaries

flashcards.question: Why should a local learning server bind explicitly to 127.0.0.1?
flashcards.answer: It limits ordinary network reachability to the same host and reduces accidental exposure while the learning example lacks a complete deployment security design.
flashcards.topic: Node.js Packages, Configuration and a Local HTTP Service
